summary: Inference-time LLM optimization can reduce API spend by 50-80% in production systems without sacrificing output quality, letting teams scale usage without proportional cost growth. The highest-leverage techniques combine prompt caching (up to 90% input cost reduction), semantic caching (60-70% hit rates on repetitive workloads), and model cascading/right-sizing. Most savings come from a handful of easy-to-medium changes that developers can ship in days, not weeks.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (KV cache reuse)
techniques.description: Reuses computed key-value tensors for repeated prompt prefixes (system prompts, few-shot examples, long context) so only new tokens are billed at full rate. Cached prefix tokens are served at a steep discount or free, with no quality loss.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on input/prefix tokens
techniques.example: Place your large static system prompt and few-shot examples at the start of every request and enable cache_control (Anthropic) or rely on OpenAI automatic prompt caching so the shared prefix is only charged once.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Stores previous query-response pairs and returns a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar (via embedding vector similarity), avoiding a model call entirely. Achieves 60-70% hit rates on FAQ-style and repetitive workloads.
techniques.savings: 40-70% reduction on total calls (68% hit rates reported)
techniques.example: Embed each incoming user question, check a Redis/GPTCache vector store for a cosine-similarity match above 0.9, and serve the stored answer instead of calling the LLM.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route easy queries to small, cheap models and escalate only hard or low-confidence cases to premium models. A tiered pipeline handles the bulk of traffic on inexpensive models.
techniques.example: Send all requests to GPT-4o-mini first; if a confidence check or validation step fails, re-route the request to GPT-4o or Claude Opus.

techniques.name: Right-Sizing the Model
techniques.description: Pick the smallest model that meets quality requirements for each task rather than defaulting to the flagship model. Many classification, extraction, and summarization tasks run fine on mini/flash tier models.
techniques.savings: 60-90% reduction vs. always using flagship models
techniques.example: Switch a sentiment-classification endpoint from GPT-4o to GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash after confirming equal accuracy on a test set.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Optimization
techniques.description: Trim verbose instructions, remove redundant context, use concise formatting, and compress retrieved documents (e.g., LLMLingua) to cut input tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Replace a 500-word rambling system prompt with a tight 120-word version and use LLMLingua to compress RAG context chunks before injection.

techniques.name: Output Token Capping & Structured Output
techniques.description: Limit max_tokens and request structured/JSON output so the model doesn't generate long, rambling responses. Output tokens are often 2-4x more expensive than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and use response_format JSON schema so the model returns only the fields you need instead of a verbose paragraph.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple prompts into a single batched request or use provider async Batch APIs that offer ~50% discounts for non-real-time workloads.
techniques.example: Submit overnight bulk summarization jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get the 50% discounted rate with a 24-hour SLA.

techniques.name: RAG Context Pruning / Reranking
techniques.description: Retrieve more candidates but rerank and pass only the top few most relevant chunks into the prompt, dramatically cutting context token volume in RAG pipelines.
techniques.example: Retrieve 20 chunks from your vector DB, rerank with a cross-encoder (e.g., Cohere Rerank), and inject only the top 3 into the prompt.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the required content (e.g., a stop sequence or completed JSON) is produced, avoiding unnecessary output tokens.
techniques.example: Set a stop sequence of '}' for JSON extraction so generation halts immediately once the object closes.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer that stores and retrieves LLM responses using embedding similarity to avoid duplicate API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); self-hosted infra costs only

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store with vector search used to build high-performance semantic caches for LLM apps; integrates with LangChain and LlamaIndex.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/mo; Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, model cascading, budgets, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; LiteLLM Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform offering request logging, caching, cost analytics, and rate limiting via a one-line proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid from ~$20/mo, Enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), prompt templating, and routing primitives.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; LangSmith paid plans from ~$39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression tool that shrinks prompts and RAG context by up to 20x while preserving task performance.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway providing semantic caching, model routing/fallbacks, load balancing, and cost/usage observability across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid from ~$49/mo, Enterprise custom

tools.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
tools.description: Managed gateway that adds caching, rate limiting, analytics, and logging in front of any LLM provider with minimal config.
tools.pricing_paid: Free to start; usage-based paid tiers

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching for static system prompts and few-shot examples (up to 90% off prefix tokens with near-zero code changes).
Right-size models: move classification/extraction/summarization tasks to mini/flash tiers after a quick quality check.
Set sensible max_tokens limits and request structured JSON output to cut expensive output tokens.
Drop in a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of repetitive/FAQ-style traffic to eliminate duplicate calls.
Add a gateway/proxy like LiteLLM or Helicone for instant cost visibility, caching, and routing without rewriting app code.
